answer: Registration scans one token per identity: a juniper block whose grain is hashed, inlaid with one marble measured to 0.01 g. Auditors draw identities at random each epoch and require the token through a gauged inlet within 10 minutes; the inlet re-measures the marble and re-scans the grain, and a mismatch or missed window zeroes that epoch weight. One token fits only one inlet at a time, so parallel audits expose a token lent to a second identity. One honest agent commissions one token once, about $40, and keeps it, while 1,000 fakes need 1,000 distinct tokens, about $40,000, none shareable.
